title: MemGPT: Towards LLMs as Operating Systems
by: Charles Packer, Sarah Wooders, Kevin Lin, Vivian Fang, Shishir G. Patil, Ion Stoica, Joseph E. Gonzalez (UC Berkeley), October 2023, v2 February 2024. Read in full from the arXiv PDF (v2).
summary: MemGPT treats the context window like a computer's main memory and outside storage like disk. The model itself moves data between them through function calls: it edits a small working context, searches past messages (recall storage) and a large archive (archival storage). A queue manager warns the model at 70% of the window and evicts old messages into a recursive summary at 100%. It beats fixed-context baselines on a recall task (DMR) and on nested lookups.
ideas: Main context has three parts: read-only system instructions, a fixed-size read/write working context, and a first-in-first-out message queue whose first item is a recursive summary of evicted messages.

Working context can only be changed through function calls; the paper's example is working_context.replace('Boyfriend named James', 'Ex-boyfriend named James'), an in-place overwrite with no history kept in that block.
Nothing is lost on eviction: every message is written to recall storage and can be searched later with paginated results.
Memory pressure: a system warning at about 70% of the window lets the model save important facts before a flush at 100% evicts about half the messages.
Function results, including errors such as 'context full', are fed back to the model so it can correct itself; a heartbeat flag lets it chain several calls before answering.
Memory edits are entirely self-directed by the model; there is no rule that decides what is kept or replaced.

Measured: Deep Memory Retrieval (DMR), a task the authors built from Multi-Session Chat with LLM-written questions and an LLM judge: GPT-4 32.1% alone vs 92.5% with MemGPT, GPT-4 Turbo 35.3% vs 93.4%. The baselines only saw a lossy summary of past sessions, not the full history. Document QA used 50 sampled questions.

Caveats: MemGPT with GPT-3.5 does poorly because function calling is weak; it often stops paging through search results too early. Later, Zep showed full-conversation context scores 94.4% on the same DMR task.

took.idea: Memory is changed only through a fixed set of named calls, and every call returns a result or an error the caller can act on
Read-only parts the agent can see but not edit
Never lose the raw record: keep every message and summarise on top of it
Avoid the in-place replace without history; a change is a new doc that supersedes the old one
